title: Reach principal two-row demands with one restored dirty spare (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof with an exact free-associative polynomial certificate and finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. One restored arbitrary dirty spare removes the principal-demand reachability obstruction over every associative unital ring, including infinite and noncommutative rings.

```text
Two demanded rows + one restored dirty spare:
  zero demand                         -> 0 source insertions
  nonzero principal left demand ideal -> 1 source insertion, at most 8 ADDs
  nonprincipal left demand ideal      -> exactly 2 source insertions
```

The new step is the eight-ADD sufficiency word from witnesses `x=a beta`, `y=b beta`, `beta=sx+ty`. It restores all original dirt columns and the source. It only requires `(1-sa-tb) beta=0`, so beta may be a zero divisor and the chosen `sa+tb` need not equal one. The necessary left-ideal invariant and two-insertion echo retain aliromman #5310 and predecessor credit.

For the polynomial demand `(1+uv,u²)` over every field, this resolves the feasibility part of Nick Petalas #5211's explicit restored-spare question. The displayed word has exact abstract price `mu_2+2c_0+2c_1+4c_2`, giving 108 at the stated prices versus the cited original two-row optimum 202. The workspace contracts differ. Eight ADDs is an upper bound, not a shortest-word or three-row tariff theorem. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

Only the six files in `research/principal-demand-dirty-spare/` are added. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19601509). Its proposed ten-ADD bound improves to eight in the first verified construction; the exact tariff remains open.

## Evidence

Before, #5211 supplies a two-row polynomial obstruction and leaves one restored spare open. After, a written ordered-ring proof and a literal full-state word establish the construction and arbitrary-ring insertion-count criterion.

At head `d20c1b062da1b4eae37db73098eab97f9a3e38c0`, local CPython 3.12.15 with the standard library passes:

- The full four-by-four identity over the free associative integer polynomial ring, with literal expected monomial orders, and its exact inverse. The commutative integer-polynomial Cohn specialization checks both directions, all nine single-gate omissions, nonzero gate coefficients and destination counts `(2,2,4)`.
- Every five-tuple `(beta,a,b,s,t)` over Z/4 and UT2(F2), respectively 1,024 and 32,768 substitutions, checking every original dirt/source column and inverse. There are 192 and 6,720 nonzero valid witnesses, including 48 and 4,704 whose chosen `sa+tb != 1`. A further 3,420 selected M2(F2) witnesses pass, including 2,160 with that inequality. These are tests of the new word; predecessor scientific results are cited without replay.
- Eight invalid-domain controls, explicit wrong-order/nonzero-residual controls, and three rejected disposable optimized-script mutations: missing restoration, wrong preparation sign and reversed multiplication.
- Both direct normal and optimized commands, timed individually at 0.277 and 0.275 seconds, and both registered commands. Each is below its 120-second timeout. These are timeout observations, not speed comparisons. Metadata/source pins, AST compilation, function-size inspection, staged whitespace and exact committed-byte/source-history checks pass.
- Official six-file export integrity and declared-input coverage pass. Read-only Git-free normal/optimized replay agrees with PATH=/nonexistent; all seven exported files, including the export manifest, remain unchanged. Generated receipts bind all six package hashes; no receipt is handwritten.

Reproduce from the repository root, substituting another CPython 3.12 path if needed:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/principal-demand-dirty-spare/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/principal-demand-dirty-spare/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/principal-demand-dirty-spare
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/principal-demand-dirty-spare --check-source-history
```

Expected markers: `PASS_PRINCIPAL_DEMAND_DIRTY_SPARE`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. All registered mathematical commands ran locally; none is deferred to CI.

## Scope, sources and limitations

The universal classification rests on the written proof. The finite polynomial certificate proves the stated algebraic identity; finite-ring substitutions corroborate the specified domains. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No shortest ADD count, complete all-price three-row tariff, native coefficient preparation, physical spare lifetime, source access/routing, precision/tape implementation, stock, compiler closure, supplier admission or complete multiplication theorem is supplied. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No selected cold replay, predecessor scientific replay, native suite, Lean or Docker run was required or run.

Canonical main was freshly fetched and remains `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. The selected record is #7000 at conditional kappa 0.00363005817; the revision-8 catalogue still describes #5599. TASK.json explicitly changes the bit-helper-contract card to this algebraic boundary question. The source-binding positive control passed and is not a selected scientific replay. SOURCES.json pins source text as historical provenance; no live external scientific input is imported.

Credit Nick Petalas #5211 for the question and cited two-row obstruction, lee-phys #5139/#5089 for the principal-ideal interface, aliromman #5310 for the finite associative-ring source-count theorem and its all-ring necessary/two-insertion arguments, krzysztofwojt #5045 for source-count/return classification, Nick Petalas #4916 for the ring-valued contract, and RossRichardson, 1337isnot1337, anthonylei, ofennell-quipex, tekuuu and the retained fanout lineage. Nick Petalas #6280 is related dyadic dual-exchange precedent. Elementary stabilization and row algebra are classical; no global literature-priority claim is made. Frozen predecessor files are unchanged.

Live open/account PRs, recent handoffs and active Discussions, all-main README searches for the object, exact word price and general-ring criterion, and merged/all-state PR searches were inspected before claiming and refreshed before committing. Cached remote coverage reports complete pagination of 846 open PRs and 7,480 Discussion records; the sparse local scan covers 222 of 10,178 tracked notes. Unpublished work and arbitrary historical diffs are outside that coverage. The sole main-predecessor source is older account PR #5211; recent account fanout results below are related comparisons, not the question source or reused main step.

## Open next questions

- Determine the exact directional tariff for the polynomial demand with a restored dirty spare. Start from the `(2,2,4)` ADD vector, preserve all three dirt columns and classify arbitrary words. No matching lower bound is supplied here.
- Bind a current physical helper boundary to this ring action and an available restored spare. First price coefficient preparation, source access, lifetimes, routing and the complete consumer. No such physical binding or favorable recursive invoice is supplied.

## Related open work

- [#7514](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7514) prices a three-row binary common-value fanout with changing tariffs across its single source call. This construction uses stationary abstract prices and arbitrary ring-valued unequal demands; it reuses none of that result and computes no common optimum.
- [#7265](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7265) proves a four-demand Boolean single-insertion ADD minimum with no spare. This result adds a restored zero-demand row to two demands over arbitrary rings and makes no competing ADD-optimality claim.
- [#7183](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7183) prices a nonprincipal three-row radical demand on a directed cycle using two insertions. The new sufficiency concerns principal two-row demands with a restored spare and unrestricted elementary row directions; no common numerical optimum is computed.
- [#1865](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1865) schedules commuting C3 fanout rewrites in a selected scalar word. This abstract ring construction supplies neither those native rewrites nor a changed paid profile or ceiling.

- [#7548](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7548) bounds completed-target rounding error for a two-factor dirty commutator. This result concerns exact ring-valued source-insertion feasibility and supplies no rounded implementation or competing error value.

The completion check read this account's other open PRs created since the CLAIM: #7548, #7549, #7550, #7551, #7552, #7553 and #7554. The adjacent rounding result is listed above; the others concern fixed phase-B packing, cactus query acquisition, dual-polar cuts, integer-gauge optimization, an ordinary four-cycle and modular phase-cache memory. None computes this principal-demand source-count criterion or a competing number. No additional computation checked another contribution.

## CI notes

**CI did not certify this package.** At unchanged head `d20c1b062da1b4eae37db73098eab97f9a3e38c0`, [run 43521997914](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43521997914), [plan job 132218321527](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43521997914/job/132218321527), failed in `Onboarding helper tests`. I read the completed checks once and inspected the actual job log. It reports `Ran 760 tests` and `FAILED (failures=1, skipped=24)`. The sole failing test is:

```text
test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record
AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found
```

The mismatch is inherited from canonical main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. I read those Git objects directly: `certificates/selected-result.json` names `make frontier7000-verify`, while `docs/ci-verification.md` still has `Current selected-family replay: #6030` and `make frontier6030-verify`. The selected record, CI document and failing test have no diff between that base and this head.

The dependent [package replay job 132220403655](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43521997914/job/132220403655) was skipped because `plan` failed. Hosted CI executed no package replay. All mathematical replay, source-binding and export evidence above remains local.

I independently inspected the failed-job logs for rohanarun's [run 42905094314, job 130140894651](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314/job/130140894651) and dillona's [run 42903313790, job 130134720799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790/job/130134720799). Each has the same sole failing test, missing-command assertion, 760-test total and 24 skips. No claim is made here about other runs whose logs were not inspected.

No fix, retrigger commit, push, shared-file edit or workflow rerun was made. Maintainer repair of main is separate from this contribution.
